thread.title: Detroit Fire Department urges residents to include fire safety in spring cleaning plans
thread.title_full: Detroit Fire Department urges residents to include fire safety in spring cleaning plans

author: N. R. Altamirano
title: Detroit Fire Department urges residents to include fire safety in spring cleaning plans
text:
The Detroit Fire Department is reminding residents on March 25 that spring cleaning is an important time to address fire safety at home. The department highlights that seasonal chores can introduce fire hazards if not handled properly and encourages the public to take preventive steps during their annual clean-up routines.
Spring cleaning matters for fire prevention because clutter, improper storage of flammable materials, and unmaintained appliances can increase the risk of household fires. The Detroit Fire Department and the National Fire Protection Association recommend that residents store gasoline and flammable liquids safely, dispose of paint-soaked rags correctly, clean clothes dryers thoroughly, and clear combustible debris from around homes.
Executive Fire Commissioner Chuck Simms said, “Fire prevention and safety education are essential year-round, because each season brings its own unique risks and challenges. Spring cleaning offers a perfect opportunity for residents to take simple steps that can prevent fires, protect their families, and make their homes safer. By being proactive today, we can reduce emergencies tomorrow.”
Fire Marshal Don Thomas also pointed out how clutter inside homes affects emergency response times. “Many people don’t think of spring cleaning as a fire safety issue, but clutter and debris inside a home are among the biggest obstacles firefighters face in an emergency. Clearing walkways, stairways, and entry points not only reduce fire hazards but also ensure firefighters can move quickly to reach those in need. Spring is the ideal time to create safer, more accessible living spaces,” Thomas said.
The department’s recommended tips include keeping exits clear; maintaining space around heat-producing equipment; removing stacks of paper or cardboard; regularly cleaning dryer lint traps as well as vents; storing flammable liquids away from heat sources; disposing of oily rags safely; checking electrical cords for damage; ensuring grills are cleaned before use and placed far from structures; testing smoke alarms monthly; replacing old alarms; storing matches or lighters out of children’s reach; packing away seasonal items safely.
Residents are encouraged by the Detroit Fire Department to use this season as an opportunity to test smoke alarms throughout their homes, review escape plans with family members, and remove any hazards that could contribute to fires. Additional information on home fire safety is available at DetroitFire.gov or through the department’s social media channels.
